art_instructions: From a child’s low-to-the-ground view, show the owl flying home in late afternoon. Place the Owl on the left third of the image, about 35% of the image height, midair and facing right toward a small cozy house in the distance; wings spread in a gentle upstroke, body slightly angled upward. She has mottled brown-and-cream feathers, large amber eyes, a small green scarf fluttering back, and a tiny cross‑body satchel; her face looks happy and focused. Put the family’s house on the right third near the horizon, small but clear: a warm-toned cottage with a short wooden fence, one round window, and a red door, nestled beside two small cedar trees, matching its earlier look. A curving dirt path runs from the bottom left foreground toward the house, with soft tufts of grass and a couple of tiny mushrooms in the near foreground to emphasize the low viewpoint. The sky is a pastel dusk gradient (peach to lavender) with a few simple clouds; lighting is diffuse and soft with minimal cel shading. Add subtle motion lines behind the owl to show flight toward home; never draw text. Keep the Korean aegyo cute style: clean monoline outlines, flat pastels with one gentle accent, and fill the full frame with simple, airy background shapes.
